BACONC "UPMAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City OILG OPINION NO. S SEP 23 ENGR. MARIO A. MONDEJAR President Office of the Surallah Federation of Senior Citizen Association Municipality of Surallah, South Cotabato Dear Engr. Mondejar: This has reference to your letter seeking guidance regarding the status of elected barangay presidents of senior citizen associations who ran in the barangay elections. As represented, you are the elected president of the Surallah Federation of Senior Citizen Associations (SUFESCA). It appears that you ran for office during the 2023 Synchronized Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections (SBKE). Ostensibly, the focal person assigned by the Surallah Municipal Social Welfare and Development Office (MSDWO)—tasked with supervising the organization—demanded and ordered all barangay presidents to resign upon the filing of a certificate of candidacy. We take cognizance of the position put forth by the MSWDO as stated in her 8 January 2024 letter. Apparently, the president of SUFECA receives an honorarium from the budget allotted to senior citizens under the MSWDO of Surallah. Hence, the directive appears to be based on the apprehension that if you are elected as a barangay official, you would receive double compensation, which is prohibited under existing laws. Under such premise, arose the following queries: Is the action of the Municipal Social Welfare and Development Office focal person legitimate and correct, although the filing of the [Certificate of Candidacy] is not listed as a basis for disqualification as prescribed in the Federation's amended Constitution and By-laws? 2. Is the elected local chapter president of the senior citizens association covered by the principle that public officials are deemed to resign upon the filing of the certificate of candidacy? 3. Assuming that the resigned barangay presidents of the senior citizens can return to their positions if they lost in the barangay election and no replacement has been voted and qualified? We shall address the foregoing issues in seriatim. On the first issue, it is worth noting that the Federation of Senior Citizens Association is an independent association duly registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission and is duly accredited with the Department of Social Welfare and Development. As such, being an independent entity, the election and term of office of "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

its elected officers, as well as the matter of vacancy or resignation, must be governed by its own internal rules or by-laws. On that score, the filing of a certificate of candidacy for an elective barangay post is not grounds for the termination of the term of the elected president of the barangay senior citizens. Accordingly, this Department opines that the act of the MSWDO focal Person appears to be improper. We are of the view that the order directing the barangay presidents to resign from their positions solely on the basis of their candidacy in the BSKE appears to be premature. It is worth noting that the prohibition on double compensation cannot be legally invoked in anticipation of a future event—in this case, being elected as a barangay official—because such a prohibition should only be applied when a public official is actually in receipt of compensation from two positions simultaneously. This is the clear import of Section 95 of the Local Government Code, which provides that: "Section 95. Additional or Double Compensation. - No elective or appointive local official or employee shall receive additional, double, or indirect compensation, unless specifically authorized by law, nor accept without the consent of Congress, any present, emoluments, office, or title of any kind from any foreign government. Pensions or gratuities shall not be considered as additional, double, or indirect compensation." Going now to the second issue, the elected local chapter president of the senior citizens association is not deemed resigned upon the filing of a certificate of candidacy, as he is not among the "elected public officials" as contemplated by the law. Coming now to the last query, this Department is of the view that the resigned barangay president of a senior citizen association can no longer return to the same position if he loses the barangay election. Resignation is "an act of an official or employee by which he or she voluntarily relinquishes in writing his or her position effective on a specific date which shall not be less than thirty (30) days from the date of such notice or earlier as mutually agreed upon by the employee and the appointing officer or authority." 1 Accordingly, as applied herewith, an officer who resigned can no longer return unless he is reelected for the same position. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. ours, By the Aut o f the etary: AN VICTOR R.
